- **A phantom lot shows itself in the sums (2026-09-23, canon 0.30.213):** when the floor has one lot more than reality, total both sides first; the phantom's grams equalled the four differences to the gram, and the four dry-downs fell from an impossible 27 percent to 21 to 23 once its grams went where the material went. The sum check is the first read of any split-truck repair.
- **The lane runs in the sandbox without wrangler (2026-09-23, canon 0.30.213):** a repair rehearses on a copy of the smoke's `.smoke-persist` sqlite (the schema at the head), wiped and refilled from the snapshot's JSON tables with Python's sqlite3 (22 tables, the big logs left empty), the file split exactly as `repair-apply.mjs` splits it, run twice with changes counted; then `wrangler dev --persist-to` that directory serves the floor effect for a screenshot. The snapshot tables come across with device_stage_files; skip record_change_log, metrc_plants and metrc_packages unless the repair reads them.
- **Generate the file, do not type it (2026-09-23, canon 0.30.213):** a repair of 45 statements is written by a small generator that reads the snapshot, asserts every expected value it will guard on, mints ids with uuid5 of names, and refuses a double quote, percent sign or dash; the generator lives in the scratchpad and the file is what lands.
- **A lot still weighing is asked about before it is repaired (2026-09-23, canon 0.30.213):** 26045 read weighing with its last tote thirty-five minutes before Patrick's note; the question tool asked whether the crew was done and whether the repair should finish the lots, and his answers went into the file and the report.
- **A 7500 mid-file is a re-run first, the cap only if it repeats (2026-09-23, canon 0.30.214):** the apply of the 45-statement repair died at statement 30 on `[code: 7500]` reading `internal error; reference = ...`, where the cap of the 14th (0.30.54) read `exceeded D1's free tier daily row write limit` under the same code. The same command run whole seven minutes later finished (1 to 29 changes=0 under their guards, 30 to 45 changes=1). Read the text, not the code: internal error is a blip and the block runs again now; the row-write text is the freeze until 00:00 UTC. Either way the guarded file re-runs whole and nothing is typed by hand.
- **The verifier proves itself on a twin before it reads the floor (2026-09-23, canon 0.30.214):** pre-versus-post verification is a script that compares every added or changed row column for column with the rehearsal database's end state and lists every other difference as floor activity; before the real post snapshot it runs on a dump of the rehearsal itself (must read VERIFIED at the full count) and on a twin with planted faults (a missing statement, a missing log row, a stray tote on a repaired lot; must read NOT VERIFIED and name each). The change log is not staged whole; the rows under the repair's reason are extracted on the device with Python and matched against the rehearsal's rows by id.
- **A partial apply leaves whole records when the file pairs each write with its log row (2026-09-23, canon 0.30.214):** the stop at 30 fell between 26040's HBN void (29) and its log row (30), so the floor stood consistent (every record either whole or untouched) with one log row owed, and the re-run wrote it. Keep every UPDATE immediately followed by its record_change_log INSERT, group statements by record, and a stop anywhere is repaired by the same command whole.
- **Read the ruling's nouns in the Admin tiles before asking (2026-09-23, canon 0.30.215):** "the data queues and csvs" are two Admin tiles, Data Queues (/admin/queues) and Pending Data Uploads (/admin/uploads, the CSVs awaiting METRC), and "their category markers" are those pages' section headings; the row checkboxes elsewhere (the interco picks, the pick lines) were a false lead. Find the surface in adminHomePage's tile list first, then ask only what the surface leaves open (what the check-all drives, how the fold behaves).
- **The differing set is the mtime set, and the final tree hash is the proof (2026-09-24, canon 0.30.216):** when the device list cannot be brought across as a file, `find -newer <the brief's file>` on the device names every file the build touched (a build starts after its brief lands), the seal must name exactly those, and the identical tree hash on both sides after the copy proves nothing else moved. No hash list needs retyping.
- **A plan-then-write refactor is read for parity, not trusted (2026-09-24, canon 0.30.216):** when a batch action splits a single action into plan and write (planVoidRecord, planUploadMark), diff the single path's body against the plan line for line and read every dedicated sibling (the manifest, receive, split and location-move marks) for the record each writes; the one difference found (the recorded filename for six kinds) went to the owner's word with the reason it does not move the floor (the pending predicates read kind and ref_id).
- **Clean up what is open with the question tool in rounds of four (2026-09-24, canon 0.30.218):** when the owed list has grown past what a message can carry, put the decisions to him four at a time with a recommended pick first (the word owed on a number, the gate findings as one accept-or-fix question, the small words as one, the stale lists as close-or-show), then the standing lists as multi-select done-or-dropped questions grouped four to a card. Every pick is logged verbatim and the lists are pruned in the same fold; a dropped item that still exists on the disk (the refused-files folder) is named as still there, not as done.
- **repair-apply --local is the rehearsal (2026-09-24, canon 0.30.218):** `node scripts/repair-apply.mjs <file> --local <persist dir>` runs the repair through the app's own splitter and apply path against the local D1 under that persist directory, so the rehearsal and the real apply share every line but the target; the local meta carries no change counts, so the rows are read with sqlite3 between runs and the state hashed before and after the second run.
- **Guard on the field you change, not on the room the lot is in (2026-09-24, canon 0.30.219):** the 26039 file guarded its UPDATE on `plant_count = 686` alone; between the snapshot it was generated from and the apply the crew unloaded Silo 4 and the lot's status moved from drying to unloaded, and the change still landed. A guard on status would have refused a repair the floor still wanted. The generator's assertions read the snapshot's state so the file is right when written; the file's guards name only what the repair moves.
- **Map what each finish writes before asking what unfinish removes (2026-09-24, canon 0.30.220):** the ruling named "the next-in-line queue record from the next process", and the three finishes write three different things (trim flips a row and creates nothing; Finish run consumes containers and completes a run whose outputs were born at line entry; Finish Pack zeroes a parent, opens a carry and completes a job whose FG items were born per line). The question tool's options carried that reading surface by surface, so his picks ruled on the real records; a custom answer ("AND we need a way to unfinish things that pasteurization finishes") earned one follow-up question, not a guess.
- **Read a reversal's landing as a story, not a count (2026-09-24, canon 0.30.221):** the smoke's D1 showed one container with two identical status log rows and another container still pasteurized after the walk; the counts alone looked wrong until the walk was read in order (consumed by run one, returned by the run unfinish, consumed again by run two, returned one at a time; the other left inside the still-finished second run). For an act that undoes another, replay the smoke's steps against the log rows in time order before calling a landing right or wrong.
- **Audit the tree before the first push, and the history too (2026-09-24, canon 0.30.223):** before a repo leaves the disk, read what is not ignored (here _to_delete/ with the refused files and RESEARCH/ with vendor documents were not), grep the tree and the history for key and token values, emails and phones, and the Admin PIN, and count the staff names; put the findings to the owner as picks (rotate the PIN after, names stay in a private repo) rather than scrubbing on the Scribe's own judgment. Read-only git (log, ls-files, check-ignore, grep) is safe in the mount; status and add are not.
- **The Scribe never holds the live PIN after a rotation (2026-09-24, canon 0.30.223):** the seed PIN stays in migration 0008 for the from-zero smoke and the Scribe's local screenshots; the live floor's PIN rotates in Admin by his hands and canon says only that it rotated. Nothing the Scribe writes needs the live PIN.
- **A first commit of a long-idle repo picks up every unignored scratch directory (2026-09-24, canon 0.30.224):** git add -A after two weeks off git swept in seven miniflare persist directories, three table-dump folders parked beside reports and a toml backup; the placeholder address stopped the push and gave a second chance. Before a first push, list the committed tree by top folder and by kind (persist, dumps, bak, sqlite, lock), fix .gitignore, git rm --cached the strays and amend. Read-only checks on the mount: git ls-tree -r HEAD, git check-ignore --no-index (tracked paths never read as ignored without it), git hash-object --path per file to prove the disk equals the commit without touching the index.
- **"Repository not found" on a private repo is a wrong account, not a missing repo (2026-09-24, canon 0.30.224):** GitHub answers not-found when the stored sign-in belongs to an account the private repository does not admit. Put the account into the address (https://ACCOUNT@github.com/ACCOUNT/repo.git) and git asks for that account's sign-in in the browser; cmdkey /delete of the generic credential did not clear it.
- **eol=lf in .gitattributes keeps the disk hashable (2026-09-24, canon 0.30.224):** his global autocrlf warned on every LF file at the first commit; without eol=lf a later checkout would rewrite the working files to CRLF and every Scribe hash would drift from the sandbox mirror. * text=auto eol=lf plus the binary kinds; the blobs stay LF, the disk stays LF.
- **A queued brief's summary in _NOW must say what the brief says before the build session starts (2026-09-24, canon 0.30.225):** a brief tells the build session that canon wins where they differ, so a _NOW line written from an earlier fork (the cube staying, 0.30.223) would have overruled the brief written from the later pick (the cube gone). Fold the pick and the brief in the same sitting, and read the _NOW sentence against the brief's law before handing the paste.
- **Survey the code before writing the fork questions (2026-09-25, canon 0.30.226):** the first trucks questions assumed the truck model of 0.7.4 and 0.30.9 (a truck lot, the road, the receive) that THE BLANK SLATE (0.30.108) had retired; his answers described a surface the questions had not offered, and the second round had to be written against the code as it stands. An Explore agent over the app's readers of the assumption in question (here one lot one HBN) costs minutes and saves a brief written against a floor that no longer exists.
- **A split at the finish keeps the downstream true (2026-09-25, canon 0.30.226):** when a record must hold what several downstream readers assume is one thing (a truck with several HBNs against one lot one HBN), let the surface collect the mixture and the finishing act normalize it into the existing shapes, rather than teaching every reader the mixture. The CSV, the packages, the trim, the cryo pools, the tiles, the reports and the sheet all keep their law.
- **A timed-out commit may have landed (2026-09-25, canon 0.30.227):** device_commit_files answered "did not respond within 190s" and the link dropped; the four files were on the disk byte for byte when the link returned. A timeout is not a failure: read the sizes and hashes before committing again, and never force.
- **The build session can land while the Scribe is blind (2026-09-25, canon 0.30.227):** brief L was built in the twelve minutes the link was down; the Scribe found the report by listing SESSION_REPORTS and the moved tree by its hash. After any link drop, list the reports and hash the tree before assuming the floor is quiet.
- **List the reports before every sitting (2026-09-25, canon 0.30.229):** he pasted brief M part one to his Code session without saying so, and the report sat eleven hours until the Scribe listed SESSION_REPORTS by time; a floor request came in the meantime. Every sitting starts with ls -t SESSION_REPORTS and the tree hash, whatever the last message said.
- **One rehearsal database per repair file (2026-09-25, canon 0.30.230):** the verifier takes its expected changes from the rehearsal's end state against the pre snapshot, so a second file rehearsed on the same database shows up as four false mismatches on the first. Rehearse each file on its own fresh copy (a from-zero local D1 plus the pre snapshot's tables), or rebuild before verifying.
- **Hand every block with its cd (2026-09-25, canon 0.30.230):** a paste of two node lines without the cd ran from System32 and found no scripts; nothing touched the database, but the sitting lost a round. The first line of every block his hands run is the cd into app/ or the repo root.
- **A void by hand can hide what METRC still holds (2026-09-25, canon 0.30.230):** the prepack Available pane lists only a released, passed package with a live ledger item; fourteen passed WPR packages were released and invisible because their ledger items had been voided (shipped, not FFZ, not real). When METRC shows more than a pane, read the ledger's voids and their reasons before the code.
- **The gate's reference file is the last gate, not the brief (2026-09-25, canon 0.30.235):** brief M was written before part one and brief N landed, so find -newer on the brief listed three slices' files; the last gate report (committed once the tree was quiet) is the reference that lists exactly the new build's files, and the identical tree hash after the copy stays the proof.
- **A Version ID with no deploy line handed: read the disk before folding (2026-09-25, canon 0.30.237):** a paste of an ID alone can be a redeploy of the gated tree, a build nobody gated, or a deploy from the stray clone at Code\gripfactoryLite (which would roll the worker back to the code of 0.30.223). Read the tree hash, the newest reports and briefs, git, and app/.wrangler/tmp's mtime (a deploy run from app/ moves it) before folding; fold a redeploy as the same code, and a build nobody gated as a gate owed.
- **A purge's note is the purger's word on the rows he meant, not on every row it swept (2026-09-25, canon 0.30.238):** the FFZ inventory purges noted shipped and not real over the lists that page drew, and those lists held cryo outputs METRC still carries active at 694; the Scribe's first read (0.30.230) took the notes as floor facts and recommended too little. Read a purge's whole detail (reconcile_notes) against the mirror, by package type and by METRC state, before recommending which voids stand.
- **git status writes the index (2026-09-25, canon 0.30.238):** it refreshes cached stat data and rewrites .git/index when it can take the lock, so under G-1 as amended it is an index-touching command. The Scribe verifies a commit with read-only plumbing only: git rev-parse, git ls-files, git hash-object --path against git rev-parse HEAD:<path>, git diff-index --cached --quiet HEAD, git show HEAD:<path>, git log; never git status, git diff or git add.
- **A repair over many rows batches by row values (2026-09-25, canon 0.30.240):** repair-apply runs one wrangler call per statement and refuses a statement over 7,500 characters (cmd.exe stops at 8,191), so 79 items at one statement each would have been 316 calls. Chunk at most 20 items a statement: the UPDATE guarded by (id, wip_package_id, metrc_tag) IN (VALUES ...) with the expected void, and each log insert selecting from VALUES (its uuid5 id, the record, the tag) only where the item stands updated under the repair's stamp; the local rehearsal (miniflare's SQLite, the engine D1 runs) takes both, and the remote apply's changes count confirms them.
- **Two briefs touching the same files build in order (2026-09-26, canon 0.30.241):** brief O and brief P both edit src/scheduling.ts, src/theme.ts and src/i18n.ts; a second build started on a tree the first is still changing gates against neither report. Hand the second paste only after the first's hand-back, and gate each against the last gate report.
- **The sandbox is ephemeral (2026-09-26, canon 0.30.242):** overnight the container was reclaimed and took the canon and app mirrors, the fold scripts, the repair generators and verifiers, the rehearsal databases and the rulings log. Rebuild from the device at a session's first gate: tar app/ (without node_modules, .wrangler, the persist folders and db_backups) with canon/, BRIEFS/, SESSION_REPORTS/ and CLAUDE.md, and git archive HEAD for the pushed baseline, both under _to_delete/scribe_tmp/ (gitignored), stage the two, unpack, npm ci. The rulings log lives on the device at RESEARCH/scribe/rulings_log.txt (gitignored); a generator or verifier worth keeping goes beside it.
- **The seal is checked; the diff is the truth (2026-09-26, canon 0.30.242):** part one's seal named twelve files and the build changed twenty-two. Diff the whole tree against the pushed baseline (git archive HEAD) and gate every file that differs, sealed or not.
- **A Scribe-direct change while a build runs is held as a patch (2026-09-26, canon 0.30.243):** the plume change was ready while his Code session worked the fix; it waited as a patch under RESEARCH/scribe/pending (gitignored, so a reclaimed sandbox cannot lose it), then went onto the quiet tree with patch -p2 after its files were verified at their pre-edit hashes, and the gate covered both. Never write into the tree while a build session is in it.
- **The plume's consumption reads from the outside in (2026-09-26, canon 0.30.243):** consumption is what the trim takes off, outline first; the first sixty cells are byproduct and the last forty are product. A goal on the plume is a line in the consumption order, so ask which side of it he means before building; the Scribe's first reading put it on the wrong side.
- **A word a legend prints is asserted in the smoke too (2026-09-26, canon 0.30.245):** renaming the plume's legend passed every unit test and failed the smoke on its Spanish check (it read consumido). Before changing a visible word, grep scripts/smoke.mjs for the word in every language, not only the tests.
- **SILO OPS, Corey's drying app, and its three rules (2026-09-26, canon 0.30.246):** Silo Ops (grip-silo.pages.dev) reads /silos/live.json out of this ERP with a read-only service token and its own SensorPush feed; what it shows as loaded is this ERP's answer. His note's rules, verbatim: one, "The pounds-per-hour water numbers are air-side inference, not a scale. As of 2026-09-26 they do not reconcile: integrating a COMPLETED turn comes out 35 to 40 percent short of the water that load had to give up, and it misses by the same fraction every time, so the method is off, not the turn. Two empty bins also measured a reproducible +2.7 gr/lb offset between the sensor pairs, which would invent roughly 1,000 lb of water over an 18 hour turn. Treat the rate curve SHAPE as real and the absolute pounds as unsettled. Do not put those numbers in a model or a board deck until Corey says the calibration closed." Two, "Moisture percentages shown against a load are computed from an assumed field moisture and the ERP weight. The meter reading is the only real number." And never touch: "Setup then Silos. The sensor role dropdowns on that screen write to the shared map and land on every signed-in device including the crew's. Everything else in the app is local to my browser and safe to poke at." So: the Scribe reads drying performance from this ERP's own records (loads, clocks, dry weights, trim results), never totals Silo Ops' pounds per hour or its computed moisture, and never opens its Setup, Silos screen; a change to /silos/live.json adds fields and never alters the ones Silo Ops reads.
- **A color is checked for red-green color blindness before it ships (2026-09-26, canon 0.30.248):** bright red against the bud green read 1.41 to 1 and 1.10 to a deuteranope, one olive; a pair that must read apart on the floor needs about 3 to 1 in lightness, not only a different hue. Simulate the pair (the Machado 2009 matrix in linear RGB) and show the owner the simulated row beside the normal one.
- **METRC appends each harvest upload to its HBN (owner, 2026-09-26, canon 0.30.249):** until the HBN is finished in METRC, every harvest CSV uploaded to it adds to it, and each upload becomes its own package. So a harvest file must never come back for a whole re-upload: one file per load, <HBN>(n).csv, and a change after upload is a note to acknowledge, never a new file. Any future re-pend law on a METRC file asks first whether METRC appends or replaces.
- **A green smoke check proves only what its fixture is (2026-09-26, canon 0.30.250):** part two's smoke asserted a truck in transit on the map, and the lot it read was an on-site lot that never rode a truck. Before trusting a new check, read the fixture's rows in the smoke's D1 (status log included). And a status the code already carries beats a proxy: in_transit said on a truck exactly, where finished and never loaded caught old rows and on-site lots too.
- **A migration with a backfill is rehearsed on the newest snapshot before its gate passes (2026-09-26, canon 0.30.254):** load db_backups' newest snapshot into a database built by the migrations before it, apply the new one, and count what the backfill did (every row reached, no repeat, what pends before and after). 0076's rehearsal is kept at /home/claude/rehearse/rehearse.py while the sandbox lives. And a column's type follows the schema's convention: weights are NUMERIC; REAL is a four byte float in Postgres.
- **Moving a lot is not voiding it; a repair by lot number totals the day first (2026-09-26, canon 0.30.255):** a finished lot standing at a space that is not a silo still shows on the silo its HBN plans (0.30.81), and an open silo load keeps a lot on its tile whatever its space or plan says; only an unload finish or a void ends it (the lot's void takes its open load and package, 0.30.116; an unload session or a batch goes by the record path /record/<table>/<id>/void, since Data Queues lists only the batch, lot and package queues). Before a repair matches app lots to METRC's by number, total the day's grams and plants on both sides: a lot weighed under a new number hides in the per-lot shortfall (0.30.230 wrote 26054's 5,421,256 g as five correction totes while 26054 stood). A snapshot that fails at its first query leaves an empty dated folder in db_backups; the newest folder with a _manifest.json is the newest snapshot.
- **A log row's reason does not say which path wrote it (2026-09-26, canon 0.30.256):** when a gate reads a new path in the smoke's D1 by its log rows, check the record as well as the reason: brief R's fix logs a claimed tag under the save's own reason, plant tags replaced, the same reason every pasted tag's create rows carry, so the smoke's five such rows were inserts and the claim rested on its unit test alone. Look for the row's create logs (field id) before counting it as an update.
- **A Version ID alone does not say a migration landed (2026-09-26, canon 0.30.257):** when a migration rides the deploy and his paste is the Version ID without the apply's lines, fold LIVE with the migration UNCONFIRMED and ask for the read-only confirm, npx wrangler d1 migrations list gripfactory-lite-grip-20260914 --env grip --remote (no migrations to apply when it landed), or the probe, or a post snapshot. The pre-push audit is read only too: git rev-parse, git ls-files (--others --exclude-standard for the new, -m for the changed, -d for the deleted) and git show HEAD:path to see whether an email or a phone is new; never git status.
- **A video from him is read as stills (2026-09-27, canon 0.30.260):** the Scribe cannot play video or hear it; a video file he attaches or stages is pulled apart with ffmpeg in the sandbox (a frame every few seconds, or at the moments he names) and the frames read as images. Ask for the file, not a link; answer from the frames and say which second each came from.
- **A push by the Scribe is one yes for one push (2026-09-27, canon 0.30.261):** G-1 now lets the Scribe push, but only after it has said in chat what the push carries (files, message, branch) and he has answered yes to that push; the yes never carries to the next one, never comes from a fold, a gate, a schedule or DEPLOY/request.json, and his preference is still the block in his hands. The Scribe's shell on his computer holds no credential of his; a push from that side needs one he mints (a fine-grained token for this repository in a git credential file under an ignored path, read by git, never printed) or the road lane's watcher pushing for it.
- **git status through the bridge strands .git/index.lock (2026-09-27, canon 0.30.264):** the device shell cannot unlink, so any git command that refreshes the index (git status in every form, git add, git commit) leaves .git/index.lock behind and his next git add or commit refuses with "index.lock: File exists". It happened twice on 2026-09-27; both locks went to _to_delete/index.lock.stale-20260927-1707 and 1707b. The 0.30.257 rule stands and is sharper: read-only git through the bridge is git rev-parse, git ls-files, git check-ignore, git show, git log; never git status. A tree question is answered by the tarball, the sandbox and the listing hash, not by git on his disk. If a lock is ever stranded, mv it to _to_delete at once.
- **A browser path in a code block reads as a command (2026-09-27, canon 0.30.264):** in this conversation a code block means "run this"; the three /record/.../void paths handed in one went straight into PowerShell (harmless, refused). A page or a route goes in plain text as an address, the site's host in front, or as the clicks (Admin, Data Queues, the x).
- **FILLING counts lots, not grams (2026-09-27, canon 0.30.264):** a silo tile reads FILLING when any weighing lot names it as Move To (fillingLots > 0), so a wet weight run opened and never weighed holds the tile at 0 lb until the lot is voided or finished; a clock (an open load) wins over it, so a silo with a load never shows the stray until the load ends. The newest snapshot answers which lot; the void is his hands.
- **The CR audit reads every sealed file, wrangler.toml too (2026-09-27, canon 0.30.276):** the gate's CR audit read src, test, migrations and scripts/smoke.mjs and missed that brief Q's build wrote app/wrangler.toml with CRLF on every line; git said so at the push ("CRLF will be replaced by LF the next time Git touches it"). .gitattributes (* text=auto eol=lf) keeps the blob LF, so the repo was clean and wrangler read the file fine, but a seal hash taken on a CRLF working copy moves the day git rewrites it. The audit set is the listing set: src, test, scripts, migrations, wrangler.toml, tsconfig.json, package.json, and the build report.
- **The Scribe cannot push from the bridge without the token file (2026-09-27, canon 0.30.276):** the device shell holds no GitHub credential (the remote is HTTPS as GrippyD, no helper in the repo, his Windows store unseen), so under G-1 the block goes to his hands until the fine-grained token, scoped to this one repository and his to mint and revoke, sits in a git-ignored file git reads by itself. github.com is reachable from the shell. The pre-push audit stays read-only: git rev-parse, git ls-files -m, -d and --others --exclude-standard, git show HEAD:path; never git status.
- **tsc alone can pass on a stale generated types file (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.278):** `worker-configuration.d.ts` is git-ignored and generated by `wrangler types`; the laptop's and every gate sandbox's copy dated from 2026-08-31, before the sheet sync vars, so `npx tsc --noEmit` passed while a fresh generation (strict vars by default, `MS_TENANT_ID` typed as the literal `"TBD"`) failed with TS2430 against the app's own `Env` declarations. Every gate now runs `npx wrangler types --no-strict-vars` before `npx tsc --noEmit`, the same command `npm run typecheck` runs once V1's fix lands. A workflow on a clean checkout has no stale file to lean on; neither should a gate.
- **The worktree from the bridge (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.278):** `git worktree list` from the bridge marks the worktree prunable because its `.git` file names a Windows path; that is the bridge's view, not a fault, and the Scribe runs no git in the worktree anyway. The worktree's files are read by path (`branches/GFLiteOpsDashboard/...`), tarred and hashed like the main folder's. Its checkout is LF as the repository keeps it; the main folder's CRLF working copies (wrangler.toml, seed/strains.csv) are the odd ones, so an app/ diff between the two must drop CRs before it means anything.
- **A slice's road from the worktree to the floor (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.280):** build in branches/GFLiteOpsDashboard; the Scribe gates on the worktree's tree (tarred by path, hashed as the LF checkout); his hands commit in the worktree (git add -A; git commit, the slice's reports riding), then in the main folder git merge --no-ff GFLiteOpsDashboard and git push; the push runs .github/workflows/deploy.yml (typecheck, vitest, d1 migrations apply, wrangler deploy) and that is the deploy; his paste is the run's result and the deploy step's Version ID; the Scribe reads main after the merge and folds LIVE. A migration slice: the pre snapshot by his hands from the main folder before the merge. A red run deploys nothing; the worker-only line by hand is the fallback. The tree hash of record is the LF checkout's (the worktree's), not the main folder's CRLF working copy's.
- **src/icons.ts is taken (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.282):** the ops map's six line icons of 2026-09-02 live there (`OPS_ICON_NAMES`, `opsIconSvg`, a 64 frame), legacy but compiled and tested by `test/ops.test.ts`; the console's fourteen line art icons are `src/consoleicons.ts`. A brief names a new file only after a listing of the tree; the Scribe's sandbox holds the gated tree, so the check is one `ls` before the file is named, not after it is handed.
- **A running clock at zero is a Start time typed ahead (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.283):** the load form accepts a Start time up to ten minutes ahead of now (`resolveLoadedAt`), and both the server and the strip's tick clamp the elapsed at zero, so the tile reads `0d 00:00:00 Running` until the typed minute arrives, then runs. Not a bug to chase; the fix, if he wants one, is no grace or a "starts at" word.
- **Reading LIVE between snapshots (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.283):** the Scribe can read a live page in his Chrome through the browser extension, read only: one tab opened on the page, the DOM's data attributes read by script, the tab closed; no form, no click on anything that writes. Used once to read Silo 3's clock zero when the newest snapshot predated the load. His word if he wants it kept as a lane or stopped.
- **Proof sheets are rendered here, not there (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.284):** a build session writes a self-contained HTML sheet; the Scribe renders it in the sandbox's headless Chromium (Playwright at `/home/claude/.npm-global`, a CommonJS module, `import pkg` then destructure; the browsers under `/opt/pw-browsers`) at device scale 2, one PNG per `section.view`, and hands the pictures. A sheet's own font tells on it: `font-family="inherit"` in the icons picks up the sheet's body font, so the sheet must use the app's font or the words lie.
- **Bare data attributes are HTML, not XML (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.284):** the console's markup writes hooks as bare attributes (`data-silo-shape`, `data-icon-rad-body`); the served page reads them, an XML parser does not. A gate that parses inline SVG as XML values the bare attributes first, or the icons carry `="1"`; the redraw round of V2 gives the two icons a value so both readers agree.
- **The answers doc holds the exact words (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.288):** RESEARCH/major_move/2026-09-27_answers.docx carries the twenty-four questions with his answers typed after them and the assumptions he let stand; canon 0.30.260 summarizes it. A brief that leans on an assumption quotes the doc's line, not the summary (the Scribe reads it with a zipfile and a regex over word/document.xml; it names people, so it stays git-ignored and out of any brief).
- **A promoted string is a new string (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.289):** a dictionary entry that lived in a footnote ("Ano de cosecha") became a section heading in V3 and its missing tilde became a hold. A gate reads the Spanish of every string a slice moves into a title, a label or a heading, not only the strings it adds; `ñ` and the accents are in house (`Tamaño`, `Teléfono`), the newer entries' bare vowels (dia, seccion) are a style the crew tolerates in running text, and a tilde that changes the word is not style.
- **A Scribe-direct fix on the worktree (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.290):** at his word ("you do it") the Scribe edits the worktree's files in place through the bridge with a python read-modify-write that asserts the file's held hash first and the single occurrence of the old text, after the same edit was made and gated on a sandbox copy; the disk's tree hash must then equal the sandbox's, so the gate's bytes are the merge's bytes. No git; the commit stays his hands. The fix report says Scribe direct in its first line.
- **A PowerShell block does not stop for a failed node script (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.291):** the V3 block ran the pre snapshot first and the snapshot threw (7403 from the D1 API), but PowerShell went on to the commit, the merge and the push, so a migration merged without its snapshot. Every block that carries a snapshot now reads `node scripts/db-snapshot.mjs <label>; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "snapshot failed, stop here" }` before the git lines, and the Scribe reads db_backups for a non-empty folder before folding a migration slice as clean. A snapshot folder can exist and be empty: the script makes the folder, then queries.
- **7403 from wrangler on his laptop (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.291):** "The given account is not valid or is not authorized to access this service" on a d1 execute --remote that worked the day before points at the credential wrangler picked, not the database: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN or CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID left in the PowerShell session (the morning's token test) override the OAuth login; Get-ChildItem env:CLOUDFLARE_* and npx wrangler whoami tell which is in use. The error prints his account id; canon never repeats it.
- **A snapshot lists the new table (2026-09-28, canon 0.30.292):** db-snapshot.mjs dumps every table sqlite_master names, so a post-migration snapshot's table list is a free confirmation that the migration landed on the remote (farm_plant_counts: 0 rows proved 0078); read it before asking him for a query. And a 7403 that clears itself under the same login minutes later is the API's passing refusal, not his credential: retry once from app/ before chasing tokens.
- **The floor's shape for the gate (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.293):** a METRC package's type is the first token of its item name before " - " (BUD, WPR, PRE, MOB, WBP, WIP, SHA, MIX, TRI, BIO, THCA; the GRIP and Mitten items are vapes and oils), its testing state is metrc_packages.lab_test_status (NotSubmitted, SubmittedForTesting, TestPassed, RetestPassed, TestFailed), and it is pasteurized when a live wip_packages row with source 'cryo' carries the tag as package_code (the cryo run's outputs are the true METRC packages; the consumed trim containers read 'pasteurized' and are archival). The InTesting sheet's table, external_test_results, is empty on the floor until MS_CLIENT_SECRET or a DROPS file feeds it; the Testing Desk's tables are empty too. A brief that draws on either says so and gives the empty words.
- **An amendment is a slice (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.293):** when he adds work in the middle of the plan, the Scribe writes it as a numbered slice with its own brief (V11 for the Maintenance node), places it in the order with his word to move it, and keeps the numbers as names, not ranks.
- **A section renders from a fixture through a throwaway test (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.294):** the console's modules import each other without extensions, so Node's type stripping cannot run them from a script; a one-off `test/zz_render_*.test.ts` in the Scribe's sandbox copy (never the worktree) that calls the section builder with a fixture and writes a page wrapped in `themeStylesheet("cerberus")` runs under `npx vitest run <file>`, and Playwright screenshots it at 1100 px and 390 px; the file is removed after. The fixture's figures are worked by hand first, so the picture proves the arithmetic as well as the look.
- **The 7403 is the first call after idle (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.295):** twice in one day wrangler's first `d1 execute --remote` after hours idle answered 7403 under a whole OAuth login, and the retry minutes later was clean; the block's guard (`if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw }`) turned it from a slipped snapshot into a stop, and the remedy is the snapshot run alone once more before the acts. A one-retry inside scripts/d1lib.mjs is the housekeeping that ends it. Every attempt leaves a folder; an empty one is a failed attempt, and the newest complete folder is the snapshot of record.
- **A stored stamp is not a string to compare (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.296):** the instrument imports keep `tested_at` as the file wrote it ("2026-09-04", "9/29/2026 10:15 AM", or "unknown"), so `tested_at > requested_at` against an ISO stamp is a lexical accident: a same-day date-only reading sorts before the stamp and "unknown" sorts after everything. Read the day (`testedDayOf`) and compare days; a row with no date answers nothing. The cure panes carry the same string compare (cure.ts) and are a later tidy.
- **The gate renders the alarm on every sheet (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.296):** a color the brief names from one picture (the waste red of the bud waffle, a filled area) can vanish as thin text on the dark sheets; the render from a fixture in CO, Lite and Spanish before the verdict is what caught it, and the fix reads the sheet's own alarm token with a fallback chain (`var(--danger, var(--alert, #8b2e2e))`). Words on a line are ordered for the reader: the countdown first, then which check, then the lot; a number between "in" and a clock reads as a quantity.
- **The fix is gated before the word and written after it (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.297):** when a gate holds, the Scribe writes the fix in a sandbox copy, runs the whole gate on it (typecheck, both zones, the smoke, the render) and hands the pictures with the hold, so his "you do it" is one write: the held hashes read on the disk once more, the gated files committed whole (no re-typing, no in-place edit on the bridge), and the tree hash on his disk read back equal to the gated tree. The fix report carries the seal of the sandbox run, since the bytes are the same.
- **The folders are the log of the morning (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.298):** his paste shows the run that succeeded; db_backups shows every attempt before it. An empty folder is a refused first call (the 7403 after idle, three mornings running), a complete folder under an older label is a retry typed from history, and the newest complete folder with the right label is the snapshot of record. The Scribe reads the folder list with the paste and names the empties for his Remove-Item; a mislabeled complete snapshot is his call, never the Scribe's to remove.
- **The worktree reads its own canon (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.299):** a build session opened in branches/GFLiteOpsDashboard reads canon/_NOW.md and BRIEFS/ from that checkout, and since THE BRANCH FOLDER (0.30.277) every commit runs there, so the main folder's canon, synced by the Scribe, was never added again and the repo's canon froze at 0.30.275 while seven briefs lived only on the disk. After every fold and every brief the Scribe copies the trio into the worktree's canon/ and the new brief into its BRIEFS/ (a cp inside the connected folder, the hashes read back), so the session reads the truth where it stands and the slice's commit carries canon and its brief to main. The main folder's canon stays the Scribe's sync target; the worktree's copy is the repo's.
- **A screen's filter is a type, and the checks follow the screen (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.300):** when he takes spaces off a screen, the filter reads the space's type (`spaceTypeOf`: silo, dry_room, freezer), never its name, so a new silo joins and a renamed room stays off; and the work the screen exists for (the aW and MC checks) narrows with it everywhere, or the crew is nagged from tiles the screen no longer shows. The render from a fixture holding one load of each kind is the proof: the screen with the silos alone, the other tiles elsewhere with their clocks and no lines, the work pane with the silo's rows only.
- **Git refuses to overwrite a working copy it did not write, identical or not (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.301):** once the branch commits canon and the briefs, the same files sitting modified or untracked in the main folder's working tree stop the merge ("Your local changes ... would be overwritten", "untracked working tree files would be overwritten", "Aborting"), even when every byte is the same. The merge aborts clean, main stays where it was, nothing deploys. The remedy is his hands: stash the copies with --include-untracked, merge, drop the stash, push. The rule that ends it: a brief is written to the worktree's BRIEFS/ only and reaches the main folder by the merge; the trio goes to the main folder as well, and every merge block runs git checkout -- canon before the merge, since the working copy is the branch's own bytes and comes straight back.
- **The repo's canon lags the disk by design now (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.302):** main HEAD carries the trio as the worktree held it at the slice's commit (0.30.300 at V12's), the main folder's working canon carries the newest fold, and the Project carries the same newest fold; the three agree only at the instant of a merge. Reading canon from the repo (a clone, a GitHub view) reads the last merged fold; reading it from the disk or the Project reads today's. A build session in the worktree reads the newest too, since the Scribe copies every fold there before it commits.
- **A pane's exit is a recorded finish, and the floor is counted before the brief (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.303):** when he says a pane shows too many, the Scribe reads the pane's law (cureMembership), names the data event that should end it (the trim schedule row's completion, not the lot's trimmed status, which the reconcile sets later or never), and counts the floor by hand on the newest snapshot under both laws before writing the brief; the brief carries his number matched exactly (11 under the old law, his four under the ruling, the seven that leave named by lot). An exit tied to a later, optional event (a container into a cryo run) leaves lots stranded on a pane forever.
- **The gate runs the built query against the floor (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.304):** when a slice changes who a pane shows, the gate lifts the built SQL out of the source (LOTS_SQL between its backticks), runs it on a database built from the migrations and loaded with the newest snapshot's tables, applies the built membership, and compares the pane's lots with the count he gave; a slice whose whole point is a number passes only when the number comes out of the built code on the real floor, not from the Scribe's hand arithmetic alone. Three small files can be staged one by one into a copy of the last gated tree; the tree hash on both sides proves the copy is the worktree.
- **The checkout before the merge is the block's own line now (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.305):** git checkout -- canon in the main folder, between the worktree's commit and the merge, discards a working copy that is the branch's own bytes and the merge returns them; after V13 main HEAD, the main folder and the worktree agreed on the trio to the byte. It costs nothing while the Scribe keeps both copies identical at every fold, and the Scribe reads all three hashes after every merge to prove it.
- **The next prompt follows the push (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.306):** his standing word, "Send the next slice prompt after each push": the LIVE fold and the next brief are one motion now; the Scribe reads the plan's next slice, reads the doc's own page for it (the Major Move PDF is on his disk under RESEARCH/, staged and read with pdftotext and a page render when the words alone leave the picture open), names the assumptions for his word inside the brief, writes it to the worktree's BRIEFS/ and hands the paste. His word stays on the assumptions and the order, not on whether to start.
- **A report change is a view change (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.307):** the page, the CSV, the XLSX and the PDF all render one ReportView, so a new column or a totals row is put on the view with a column flag (grams, lbs) or a row flag (_total) and every export carries it by itself; the brief names the figures from his screenshot worked by hand (the total's pounds from the total's grams, the two ways checked to agree) so the test pins the same numbers he sees. When the chat's card cannot be delivered (the upload answering 500), the brief still lands on his disk and its words go into the canon row.
- **Two slices, one gate, one commit (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.308):** when his Code session builds two briefs in sequence on one worktree tree and hands them together, the Scribe gates the combined tree once (the union of the two seals against the last gated tree, the later build's hashes superseding the earlier's on the files both touched, theme and smoke here) and hands one commit for both, since the tree the checks passed on is the tree that merges; the report says which seal each file belongs to. The arithmetic a slice draws (a bar's shares, a report's totals) is worked by hand on a fixture before the code's numbers are read, so the code is checked against the hand and never the reverse.
- **The 7403 refusal follows idle time, not the morning (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.309):** the fifth refused first call came at 15:03, six hours after the morning's snapshot of 08:57, so the pattern is the first D1 call after an idle stretch; the guard stopped the block, the snapshot line alone answered 25 seconds later, and the acts ran. Every merge block keeps the guard and the words "run the snapshot line alone once more"; the empty folder is the failed attempt, his Remove-Item; the d1lib one-retry housekeeping stays offered for the day he wants the refusal absorbed.
- **One number for the day rides the farm table as ALL (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.310):** when his word turns a per-farm figure into one entry for the day (the harvest hours, a travelling crew), the brief keeps the table (harvest_labor_hours, UNIQUE farm_code and work_date) and writes the one entry as farm_code ALL, the ALL row winning over the sum of the farm rows and past days reading as they did, because the sheet sync still lands per farm and a new table would give the same number two homes. A plan's estimate of a migration is an estimate; the brief says when the read finds none is needed and the pin stays. The live pane's DOWN timer reuses the strip's [data-clock] script already on the page rather than a second ticker.
- **A color named by another element's is checked on every sheet (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.311):** when a brief says a new mark takes the waffle's colors (or any element's), the gate renders the three sheets and reads the theme's values per sheet, because a build reaches for the first sheet's hex and the third sheet's element wears another; the fix is the theme variable or the sheet's own value, never one hex for all. The RUNNING law of 0.30.163 (a queued lot with a shift on duty) now also decides when a live pane may say DOWN, so a timer that never appears while a lot waits is the law working, not a bug; his word decides whether the queue clause belongs on a live pane.
- **The snapshot's file count moves with the migrations (2026-09-29, canon 0.30.312):** a pre snapshot holds one file per table plus the manifest, so its count is the table count of the floor at that instant: 74 files before 0081 applied (73 tables), 75 after (fulfillment_overrides among them). A count that steps up by the new tables of the last merge is the snapshot working, not a stray file; a count that steps down is the question. The idle refusal held at three and a half hours as at six, so the guard and the second snapshot line stay in every block.
- **"do it" on a list of observations is the Scribe-direct slice (2026-09-30, canon 0.30.313):** when the gate passes with observations and his word is "do it", the Scribe applies the observations' remedies itself under the V11 pattern: a fix script with one anchored replacement per change and an assertion for every value it claims (the sheet's waffle pair read from the sheet before the bar takes it), the sandbox copy gated in full (typecheck, both zones, the smoke, renders), then the files written whole to his disk through the bridge and read back equal, then the fix report, the fold and the block. A live pane's DOWN follows the doc's own clock (thirty idle minutes on the scale); a ruling about the cards' RUNNING (0.30.163) is not carried onto a pane the doc gave its own law.
- **The idle refusal has a threshold, not a certainty (2026-09-30, canon 0.30.314):** the first D1 call after idle refused at 3 h 25 min and at 6 h and answered at 2 h 20 min, so a block run within a couple of hours of the last snapshot may simply work; the guard and the words "run the snapshot line alone once more" stay in every block regardless, since the cost of the guard is nothing and the cost of a merge without a fresh snapshot is the rule of 0.30.301 broken. A snapshot folder list with no empty folder after a merge is the guard not firing, not the guard missing.
- **A floor intervention is read from the newest snapshot before a word is written (2026-09-30, canon 0.30.315):** the crew's message names lots and figures; the Scribe reads the snapshot on his disk table by table (the lots, the totes, the dry rows, the loads, the sessions, the born packages, the plant tags, the change log filtered by the record ids) and finds the origin in canon (here the repair of 0.30.180, done on his ruling of what METRC held). The app follows METRC's plants, never the other way, so the fix is the app's records on METRC's shape and the one fact the Scribe cannot see (what METRC holds) is asked as a yes or no with both files rehearsed before the answer. A repair that touches an unloaded lot writes the born package's newest inv_unload_adjust row last, because the package_adjustments file reads that row alone; a repair file lives in the worktree and is applied from the worktree's app while the snapshots run from the main folder's app (ROOT_DIR is the folder above app/).
- **A repair is not done until the post snapshot is read back (2026-09-30, canon 0.30.316):** his word after an apply can be three words ("should be good"); the Scribe reads the post snapshot on his disk against the rehearsal's verify (every header, row count, package qty, void stamp and log row, the change log's row count up by exactly the file's inserts) before folding it as applied, and the shape he ran answers the question he was asked (Shape B run means METRC has no harvest 26029). The empty pre folder before a landed pre is the refusal pattern of 0.30.309, now seven times.
- **A ruling written as a screen is read against the records it touches (2026-09-30, canon 0.30.317):** his harvest-node ruling names panes, comboboxes and buttons; the brief maps each to the record it reads or writes (the HBN select to harvest_batches by farm with the farm-day rule, "scheduled" to the Internal Logistics pass row, "exposed" to the Dry Queue, a load to a new table with the tote carrying its id, an HBN's lot minted at the first tote), names the words in both languages because he asked for the warnings in Spanish, and puts every choice the screen leaves open (the destination farms, the holding space, the plant count, what "<<" undoes) in the assumptions for his word. A new node that shares a ledger with an old one (wet_weights) keeps the old node's files and split untouched by adding a column, never by changing the lot's shape.
- **A brief names one law per select, and the gate reads the ruling before the SQL (2026-09-30, canon 0.30.318):** the V15 brief put the ruling's sentence (a finished HBN leaves the combobox) and an existing rule's name (the farm-day rule of NO_FINISHED_LOT_SQL) in the same paragraph, and the build followed the rule, so a finished HBN stayed on the select and took weight past the warning that promised it would not. The ruling wins; a brief that cites a rule by name says whether it applies or is replaced, in one sentence, and the gate checks the screen's promises (a warning's words are law) against the code, not the build report's assertion. On the screen: a page built as station-triple gets equal thirds from the chrome rule at the end of every sheet, whatever the working pane's own flex says; a station whose middle pane holds a six-column table names its own weighting; overflow on a flex item with a zero basis collapses it in the phone column, so the overflow goes on a wrapper inside the pane; a flex form inside a table cell wraps its controls into tall rows, so the controls that a change needs stay hidden until the change; and a class borrowed from another pane (queue-pane-item) carries no rule outside it.
- **The worktree takes a fix by day; the push waits for the crew's night (2026-09-30, canon 0.30.319):** the push is the deploy, so while the crew is harvesting on the live app nothing merges, but the worktree is a folder on his disk and a gated fix lands there whenever it is ready (files written whole, hashes read back, the tree hash equal to the gated one), the merge block standing in the gate report for his hands after hours. His word on a fix can be a word about its pictures ("the preview looks solid"). The wait is spent on the next brief that nothing blocks, its paste held until the push, because a slice builds on the branch only after the one before it is merged.
- **A ruling on a slice not yet merged is briefed onto the worktree as it stands and rides with that slice (2026-09-30, canon 0.30.320):** his housekeeping on V15 came while V15 waited for the night's merge; the brief names the worktree's tree, its own migration number after the slice's (0083 after 0082), and rides with the same commit after its own gate, so the crew learns one rule, not two. The read of such a ruling maps each of his nouns to a record already there (the in-transit list to the Loads sent pane, the silo scheduler to the Dry Queue, the HBN/Lot tag to the HBN's weighing lot, "schedules it" to the >> pass) and says the mapping back to him in chat so he can catch it; a rule that must tell two finishes apart (the crew's YES and the scheduler's pass) gets a column on the record the crew's word is about (field_closed_at on the batch), never a status the transition graph does not know.
- **A brief written ahead of its turn names what it builds on and holds its paste (2026-09-30, canon 0.30.321):** while a merge waits for the crew's night, the next unblocked brief is written from its sources (the doc's words and his answers, read from RESEARCH/ on his disk and quoted verbatim into the brief, never the crew's names), its migration numbered after every migration ahead of it in the queue (0084 after V15.1's 0083), its opening naming the merge it follows, and its paste held until that push lands, because a slice builds on the branch only after the one before it is merged. An interactive builder the doc draws (lines added before a save) is the page's script over a plain form, the server the only judge of the record.
- **A select's law is read against the floor's own rows before a brief names it (2026-09-30, canon 0.30.322):** the V15.1 brief wrote the field select as the crew's close alone, and the build followed it; the gate ran that clause on the newest snapshot and found twenty-eight HBNs finished weeks ago, because harvest_batches.status is open forever and says nothing about a harvest being done. The gate's own snapshot check (the clause bound to today, counted) is part of every gate on a pick list from now on, and a brief that changes a pick list's law names what the floor's rows would show under it. The composed law (the crew's close AND the farm-day rule) is the one V15 was built with plus the ruling's close, so a fix that replaces a rule keeps what the rule was quietly doing.
- **"Push everything" is one commit, and the canon in it is the version folded last (2026-09-30, canon 0.30.323):** when several gated pieces wait on one merge (a slice, its fix, a follow-on slice, its fix), his word to push is the word on every pending landing, the files land first (hashes read back, the tree equal to the last gated one), the canon trio is folded and copied into the worktree's canon/ before he commits so the repo's canon matches the disk's, and the commit message names every piece and that canon version. The block stays his hands: the worktree's git does not answer the bridge and the credential is his.

## How the owner likes to work

- Terse, no recaps, reads diffs. Address by name.
- He answers pickers in free text when the options miss; parse the text as the ruling and fold it. He also delegates ("make a recommendation") and expects the Scribe to pick and own it.
- Focused questions through AskUserQuestion get rich answers; he answers partially and lets the rest ride; proceed on what is answered.
- He supplies the current tool per box. The Scribe never designs ahead of the open box and calls out drift, his or its own. "Stop and talk through every box."
- "Orange barrel that" = defer and track. Operator vocabulary (HBN, CSA/CSB, aW, MOB): ask, do not guess.
- No flubdubs. Screens fill with real operations.
